answer: Each identity posts a 70-credit quorum bond in the juniper registry, co-signed by seven verifiers from a rotating pool. No verifier set can be reused: the registry rejects any bond reusing those signatures. The tide rotation reseats the committee each epoch, and the ocean audit samples 5% of bonds, slashing stakes on any reused signature. The first 100 identities pay 70 each; scarcity raises the fee by 10 per 100, so the 1,000th fake costs 160 and 1,000 fakes lock 115,000 credits. A rented-quorum ring fails on reused signatures. An honest agent posts one 70-credit bond.
